text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Prevention of Corruption Act 1961 is to be amended to give the Anti-Corruption Agency more clout in combating graft, syndicated crime and money laundering.

- The Cabinet on Wednesday advised all government agencies to refrain from conducting open burning when disposing of confiscated materials in public. Instead, the agencies should look for more environmentally-friendly methods, it said.

- The Securities Commission (SC) has announced five policy changes aimed at making the Malaysian capital market more attractive to local and foreign institutional investors. The measures include reduction of supervisory overlap and the merger of the SC and the Commodities Trading Commission.

- Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation and its counterpart in Peru, Prompex, will sign an agreement formalising cooperation between the two organisations next week during the state visit of Peru President Alberto Fujimori to Malaysia.
- The Criminal Procedure Code will be amended to revert to prima facie as the standard of proof required at the end of the prosecution's case in criminal trials.
